title: Finnish

proverbOfDay.context: A beloved Finnish encouragement for learners mastering complex grammar: persistent grit and sisu always lead to triumph.

cultureTips.title: The Sauna Sanctuary (Saunarituaali)
cultureTips.description: Finland boasts over 3 million saunas for 5.5 million citizens. It is a tranquil, egalitarian sanctuary for physical and mental cleansing. Etiquette: shower first, remove footwear, relax without judgment, and ask before tossing 'löyly' (water onto hot stones).

cultureTips.title: The Spirit of 'Sisu' (Perseverance Against Odds)
cultureTips.description: Sisu is Finland's defining cultural soul: stoic determination, quiet courage, and unbroken grit when facing formidable challenges. It means pushing through sub-zero winters or tough exams with quiet resolve rather than loud boastfulness.

cultureTips.title: Comfort with Silence (Hiljaisuus on kultaa)
cultureTips.description: In Finnish social codes, conversational pauses are natural marks of thoughtful contemplation and respect, not 'awkward silence'. Finns listen with full attention until you finish speaking and don't feel compelled to fill pauses with idle chatter.

cultureTips.title: Summer Cottage Escapism (Mökkikulttuuri)
cultureTips.description: During summer, cities empty out as Finns retreat to rustic lakeside cabins (mökki). Life revolves around chopping firewood, fishing, swimming in pristine lakes, harvesting berries, and disconnecting from digital stress.

cultureTips.title: Everyman's Right (Jokamiehenoikeus)
cultureTips.description: Ancient legal custom grants everyone the freedom to roam wild forests, paddle pristine lakes, forage wild bilberries (mustikka) and chanterelles, and pitch a tent overnight—provided you protect nature and leave zero trace.

cultureTips.title: The Birch Whisk Sauna Ritual (Vihta / Vasta)
cultureTips.description: In the summer sauna, fresh birch twigs bundled together with twine are used to gently whisk the skin. The leaves release fragrant essential oils, improve blood circulation, and open pores.

questions.prompt: How many letters are in the standard Finnish alphabet (including Å, Ä, and Ö)?
questions.explanation: The Finnish alphabet has 29 letters: 26 standard Latin letters plus Å, Ä, and Ö.

questions.prompt: How is the Finnish letter 'J' pronounced?
questions.explanation: In Finnish, 'j' is always pronounced like the English 'y' in 'yes' (e.g. 'juna' sounds like 'yoo-nah').

questions.prompt: Match the special Finnish vowels to their pronunciation sounds:

questions.explanation: 'Äiti' (mother) starts with the front vowel Ä, pronounced like 'a' in 'cat'.
The word 'kissa' (cat) begins with the letter K.

questions.prompt: What happens when a Finnish vowel is written double (e.g. 'aa', 'uu', 'ii')?
options: It is held twice as long and can change the word's meaning
It is pronounced with a higher pitch only
It turns into an English sound
questions.correctAnswer: It is held twice as long and can change the word's meaning
questions.explanation: Double vowels (kaksoisvokaalit) are held twice as long. Compare 'tuli' (fire) vs 'tuuli' (wind)!

questions.prompt: Match words that differ only by vowel length (single vs double vowel):
Listen to the word 'Yö' (night). What two special vowels make up this word?
questions.explanation: 'Yö' means 'night' in Finnish, composed of the two front vowels Y and Ö.

questions.prompt: What happens with double consonants (e.g., 'kk', 'pp', 'tt') in Finnish?
options: There is a short pause / stop before release
questions.correctAnswer: There is a short pause / stop before release
questions.explanation: Double consonants have a distinct stop: 'kuka' (who) vs 'kukka' (flower).
'Yö' is the Finnish word for night.

questions.prompt: Match Finnish letters with example words:
Listen to the country name 'Suomi'. How is the letter 'S' pronounced?
questions.explanation: Finnish 's' is always crisp and voiceless, never buzzing like English 'z'.

questions.prompt: Which of these vowels are back vowels in Finnish vowel harmony?
questions.explanation: A, O, and U are back vowels, while Ä, Ö, and Y are front vowels. E and I are neutral.

questions.prompt: Match the vowel types in Finnish vowel harmony:

questions.explanation: 'Pöllö' (owl) is a great example of the front rounded vowel Ö.

questions.prompt: Listen to the word 'Pöllö' (owl). Which vowel repeats twice?
questions.explanation: 'Pöllö' contains two 'ö' sounds.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Finnish language alphabet'
questions.explanation: 'Suomen kielen aakkoset' means 'The Finnish language alphabet'.

questions.prompt: In Finnish, is every letter pronounced consistently as written (phonetic orthography)?
options: Yes, Finnish is almost completely phonetic
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, Finnish is almost completely phonetic
questions.explanation: Finnish has one of the most transparent phonetic spelling systems in the world: you read each letter almost exactly as it is written!
